text.p: French basketball got a major boost on Wednesday when two Frenchman were drafted by National Basketball Association teams, a spokesman for the NBA in Europe said on Thursday.

Olivier St Jean was the 11th pick and has joined the Sacramento Kings direct from American college basketball with San Jose State, while international guard Alain Digbeu will leave Villeurbanne for the Atlanta Hawks after being picked 50th in the draft.

The NBA's European spokesman, Ray Lalonde, was especially pleased for St Jean. "This is a surprise and great news. It's quite an accomplishment to be drafted 11th after only three years of college basketball," he said.
St Jean, who left France as a junior in 1993, began his college career at Michigan University before moving on to San Jose State.
The 22-year-old forward (1.98 m, 103 kg) was the leading scorer in the Western Athletic Conference last season..
Digbeu, also 22, played for Villeurbanne in the European Final Four last season but is missing the current European championship in Spain because of injury.
Villeurbanne coach Gregor Beugnot told French radio he hoped his club could come to an agreement with the Hawks so that Digbeu could play for another season in France before joining the NBA.
"Alain's departure will leave an enormous void in the team. He has extraordinary qualities," he said.
The French pair were among nine non-Americans in the draft, but it is not the first time a Frenchman has been drafted by the NBA.
In 1960, the 2.18-metre Jean-Claude Lefevre was picked by the Los Angeles Lakers only to then opt to play for France in the Olympic Games.
